chapter_sections.label: Definition:
chapter_sections.text:
A QUADRILATERAL is a closed figure with four sides, four angles and four vertices.
A PARALLELOGRAM is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

chapter_sections.label: Key Points:
points: A quadrilateral has four sides, four angles and four vertices.
In a parallelogram, both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles.
Special parallelograms:
RECTANGLE  — a parallelogram in which one angle is a right angle.
RHOMBUS    — a parallelogram with all four sides equal.
SQUARE     — a parallelogram with all four sides equal and one angle 90 degrees.

chapter_sections.label: LIST OF TOPICS IN THIS CHAPTER:
items: - Topic 8.1: Properties of a Parallelogram
- Topic 8.2: The Mid-point Theorem
- Topic 8.3: Summary

items.question: What is a quadrilateral? Name its elements.
items.answer:
A QUADRILATERAL is a closed figure with four sides, four angles and four vertices.
Its elements are: four sides (AB, BC, CD, DA), four angles (angle A, angle B, angle C, angle D) and four vertices (A, B, C, D).
The sum of all four angles of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees.

items.question: What is a parallelogram? Name three special types of parallelograms.
items.answer:
A PARALLELOGRAM is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
Three special types:
(i)  RECTANGLE — a parallelogram in which one angle is a right angle (90 degrees).
(ii) RHOMBUS   — a parallelogram in which all four sides are equal.
(iii) SQUARE   — a parallelogram in which all four sides are equal and one angle is 90 degrees.

items.question: State the Mid-point Theorem.
items.answer:
Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.8):
The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
If E and F are mid-points of AB and AC in Triangle ABC, then:
EF || BC  and  EF = (1/2) BC.

items.question: State the converse of the Mid-point Theorem. (Theorem 8.9)
items.answer:
Converse of Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.9):
The line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.
That is, if E is the mid-point of AB and EF || BC, then F is the mid-point of AC.

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 65 degrees. Find all four angles. State the properties used.
items.answer:
Step 1: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram, angle A = 65 degrees.
Step 2: angle C = angle A = 65 degrees.
(Reason: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal — Theorem 8.4)
Step 3: angle A + angle B = 180 degrees.  (Co-interior angles, AD || BC)
65 + angle B = 180 degrees.
angle B = 180 - 65 = 115 degrees.
Step 4: angle D = angle B = 115 degrees.  (Opposite angles are equal)
Answer: angle A = 65 degrees, angle B = 115 degrees, angle C = 65 degrees, angle D = 115 degrees.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D and E are mid-points of AB and AC respectively. If DE = 4.5 cm, find BC. Also find the perimeter of Triangle ADE if AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm.
items.answer:
Step 1: Given: D and E are mid-points of AB and AC. DE = 4.5 cm.
Step 2: By Mid-point Theorem, DE = (1/2) BC.
So, BC = 2 x DE = 2 x 4.5 = 9 cm.
Step 3: Since D is mid-point of AB: AD = (1/2) x AB = (1/2) x 8 = 4 cm.
Since E is mid-point of AC: AE = (1/2) x AC = (1/2) x 6 = 3 cm.
Perimeter of Triangle ADE = AD + DE + AE = 4 + 4.5 + 3 = 11.5 cm.

items.question: Prove that a diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles. (Theorem 8.1)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a parallelogram. AC is a diagonal.
TO PROVE: Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
PROOF:
Step 1: In parallelogram ABCD, BC || AD and AC is a transversal.
Therefore, angle BCA = angle DAC.  (Alternate interior angles)
Step 2: Also, AB || DC and AC is a transversal.
Therefore, angle BAC = angle DCA.  (Alternate interior angles)
Step 3: AC = CA.  (Common side)
Step 4: By ASA congruence rule:
Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
Therefore AB = DC and AD = BC.  (CPCT)
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: Prove that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. (Theorem 8.6)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a parallelogram. Diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.
TO PROVE: OA = OC and OB = OD.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AOB and Triangle COD:
AB || DC and BD is a transversal.
Therefore, angle OAB = angle OCD.  (Alternate interior angles)
Step 2: AB || DC and AC is a transversal.
Therefore, angle OBA = angle ODC.  (Alternate interior angles)
Step 3: AB = CD.  (Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal — Theorem 8.2)
Step 4: By ASA congruence rule:
Triangle AOB is congruent to Triangle COD.
Therefore, OA = OC and OB = OD.  (CPCT)
Hence, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which P, Q, R and S are mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. AC is a diagonal. Show that PQRS is a parallelogram.
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a quadrilateral. P, Q, R, S are mid-points of AB, BC, CD, DA. AC is a diagonal.
TO PROVE: PQRS is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle ABC, P is mid-point of AB and Q is mid-point of BC.
By Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.8):
PQ || AC  and  PQ = (1/2) AC.  ... (1)
Step 2: In Triangle ACD, S is mid-point of DA and R is mid-point of CD.
By Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.8):
SR || AC  and  SR = (1/2) AC.  ... (2)
Step 3: From (1) and (2): PQ || SR  and  PQ = SR.
Step 4: In quadrilateral PQRS, one pair of opposite sides (PQ and SR) is both equal and parallel.
Therefore, PQRS is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.

---

items.question: (a) Prove that in a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal. (Theorem 8.4)
items.answer:
PART A — Proof that opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal (Theorem 8.4):
GIVEN:    ABCD is a parallelogram.
TO PROVE: angle A = angle C  and  angle B = angle D.
PROOF:
Step 1: By Theorem 8.1, diagonal AC divides parallelogram ABCD into two congruent triangles:
Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.  (ASA rule, proved in Theorem 8.1)
Step 2: From CPCT: angle ABC = angle CDA.
That is, angle B = angle D.
Step 3: Similarly, diagonal BD divides ABCD into Triangle ABD and Triangle CDB.
By the same argument (AB || DC, AD || BC, BD common):
Triangle ABD is congruent to Triangle CDB.  (ASA rule)
From CPCT: angle DAB = angle BCD.
That is, angle A = angle C.
Step 4: Therefore, opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
HENCE PROVED.

PART B — Finding all angles and verifying diagonal bisection:
Step 1: Given angle A : angle B = 2 : 3.
Let angle A = 2x and angle B = 3x.
Step 2: In a parallelogram, consecutive angles are supplementary:
angle A + angle B = 180 degrees.
2x + 3x = 180 degrees.
5x = 180 degrees.
x = 36 degrees.
Step 3: angle A = 2 x 36 = 72 degrees.
angle B = 3 x 36 = 108 degrees.
angle C = angle A = 72 degrees.  (Opposite angles are equal)
angle D = angle B = 108 degrees.  (Opposite angles are equal)
Step 4: Verification — Diagonal bisection:
Given AC = 12 cm and BD = 8 cm.
By Theorem 8.6 (diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other):
OA = OC = AC / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6 cm.
OB = OD = BD / 2 = 8 / 2 = 4 cm.
Answer: angle A = 72 degrees, angle B = 108 degrees, angle C = 72 degrees, angle D = 108 degrees.
OA = OC = 6 cm, OB = OD = 4 cm.

items.question: A figure with four sides, four angles and four vertices is called a:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: A quadrilateral has exactly four sides, four angles and four vertices.

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, if AB = 7 cm and BC = 5 cm, then CD equals:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal. So CD = AB = 7 cm.

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. If AC = 14 cm and BD = 10 cm, then OB equals:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. So OB = BD/2 = 10/2 = 5 cm.

items.question: Which of the following is true for ALL parallelograms?
items.answer: D
items.explanation: In every parallelogram, opposite sides are equal (Theorem 8.2). The other options apply only to special parallelograms.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D and E are mid-points of AB and AC respectively. If the perimeter of Triangle ABC is 36 cm and DE = 6 cm, find BC and the perimeter of Triangle ADE.

options.A: BC = 12 cm, perimeter of ADE = 18 cm
options.B: BC = 12 cm, perimeter of ADE = 9 cm
options.C: BC = 6 cm, perimeter of ADE = 18 cm
options.D: BC = 12 cm, perimeter of ADE = 12 cm

items.answer: A
items.explanation: (A) BC = 12 cm, perimeter of ADE = 18 cm is correct as per the textbook.

items.question: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is the mid-point of AB and F is the mid-point of CD. The line segments AF and CE divide diagonal BD in the ratio:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: As proved in Exercise 8.2 Q5, AF and EC trisect diagonal BD, so each trisection point divides BD such that BP = PQ = QD where P and Q are the intersection points. Each segment is 1/3 of BD.

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
A PARALLELOGRAM is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
RECTANGLE: A parallelogram in which one angle is a right angle.
RHOMBUS: A parallelogram in which all four sides are equal.
SQUARE: A parallelogram in which all four sides are equal and one angle is 90 degrees.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Theorem 8.1: A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles.
Theorem 8.2: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal.
Theorem 8.3: If each pair of opposite sides of a quadrilateral is equal, then it is a parallelogram. (Converse of Theorem 8.2)
Theorem 8.4: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal.
Theorem 8.5: If in a quadrilateral, each pair of opposite angles is equal, then it is a parallelogram. (Converse of Theorem 8.4)
Theorem 8.6: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
Theorem 8.7: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then it is a parallelogram. (Converse of Theorem 8.6)
In a rectangle, diagonals bisect each other and are equal.
In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other at right angles.
In a square, diagonals bisect each other at right angles and are equal.
Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary (add up to 180 degrees).

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - No sub-topics. (Book has only Topic 8.1 with no further sub-divisions.)
THEOREM: 8.1
STATEMENT: A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles.
GIVEN: ABCD is a parallelogram; AC is a diagonal.
TO PROVE: Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
PROOF:
Step 1: BC || AD and AC is a transversal.
So, angle BCA = angle DAC  (Pair of alternate angles)
Step 2: AB || DC and AC is a transversal.
So, angle BAC = angle DCA  (Pair of alternate angles)
Step 3: AC = CA  (Common side)
Step 4: Therefore, Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA  (ASA rule)
Hence AB = DC and AD = BC  (CPCT)
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.2
STATEMENT: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal.
GIVEN: ABCD is a parallelogram.
TO PROVE: AB = DC and AD = BC.
PROOF:
Step 1: By Theorem 8.1, diagonal AC divides parallelogram ABCD into two congruent triangles ABC and CDA.
Step 2: The corresponding sides are equal (CPCT).
So, AB = DC and AD = BC.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.3
STATEMENT: If each pair of opposite sides of a quadrilateral is equal, then it is a parallelogram.
GIVEN: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = CD and AD = BC.
TO PROVE: ABCD is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: Draw diagonal AC.
Step 2: In Triangle ABC and Triangle CDA:
AB = CD  (Given)
AD = BC  (Given)
AC = CA  (Common)
So, Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA  (SSS rule)
Step 3: Therefore, angle BAC = angle DCA and angle BCA = angle DAC  (CPCT)
Step 4: These are alternate angles, so AB || CD and AD || BC.
Step 5: Hence ABCD is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.4
STATEMENT: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal.
GIVEN: ABCD is a parallelogram.
TO PROVE: angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.
PROOF:
Step 1: By Theorem 8.1, diagonal AC divides ABCD into two congruent triangles ABC and CDA.
Step 2: From CPCT: angle ABC = angle CDA, so angle B = angle D.
Step 3: Similarly, using diagonal BD: angle A = angle C.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.5
STATEMENT: If in a quadrilateral, each pair of opposite angles is equal, then it is a parallelogram.
GIVEN: In quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.
TO PROVE: ABCD is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: angle A + angle B + angle C + angle D = 360 degrees  (Angle sum of quadrilateral)
Step 2: Since angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D:
2(angle A) + 2(angle B) = 360 degrees
angle A + angle B = 180 degrees
Step 3: Since angle A + angle B = 180 degrees, and these are interior angles on the same side, AD || BC.
Step 4: Similarly, angle A + angle D = 180 degrees, so AB || DC.
Step 5: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so ABCD is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.6
STATEMENT: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
GIVEN: ABCD is a parallelogram; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.
TO PROVE: OA = OC and OB = OD.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AOB and Triangle COD:
angle OAB = angle OCD  (Alternate angles, as AB || DC and AC is transversal)
angle OBA = angle ODC  (Alternate angles, as AB || DC and BD is transversal)
AB = CD  (Opposite sides of parallelogram — Theorem 8.2)
Step 2: So, Triangle AOB is congruent to Triangle COD  (ASA rule)
Step 3: Therefore, OA = OC and OB = OD  (CPCT)
Step 4: Hence O is the mid-point of both diagonals; i.e., the diagonals bisect each other.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.7
STATEMENT: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then it is a parallelogram.
GIVEN: In quadrilateral ABCD, diagonals AC and BD bisect each other at O. So OA = OC and OB = OD.
TO PROVE: ABCD is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AOB and Triangle COD:
OA = OC  (Given)
OB = OD  (Given)
angle AOB = angle COD  (Vertically opposite angles)
Step 2: So, Triangle AOB is congruent to Triangle COD  (SAS rule)
Step 3: Therefore, angle OAB = angle OCD  (CPCT)
These are alternate angles, so AB || CD.
Step 4: Similarly, using Triangles AOD and COB, BC || AD.
Step 5: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so ABCD is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.
EXAMPLES: (Textbook Examples — Topic 8.1)
EXAMPLE 8.1.1: Each angle of a rectangle is a right angle
PROBLEM: Show that each angle of a rectangle is a right angle.
SOLUTION:
Step 1: A rectangle is a parallelogram in which one angle is a right angle.
Let ABCD be a rectangle in which angle A = 90 degrees.
We have to show that angle B = angle C = angle D = 90 degrees.
Step 2: We have AD || BC and AB is a transversal.
So, angle A + angle B = 180 degrees  (Interior angles on the same side of the transversal)
But angle A = 90 degrees.
So, angle B = 180 degrees - 90 degrees = 90 degrees.
Step 3: Now, angle C = angle A and angle D = angle B  (Opposite angles of the parallelogram)
So, angle C = 90 degrees and angle D = 90 degrees.
ANSWER: Each of the angles of a rectangle is a right angle.
EXAMPLE 8.1.2: Diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other
PROBLEM: Show that the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other.
SOLUTION:
Step 1: Let ABCD be a rhombus. So AB = BC = CD = DA.
Let diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.
Step 2: In Triangle AOD and Triangle COD:
OA = OC  (Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other — Theorem 8.6)
OD = OD  (Common)
AD = CD  (All sides of a rhombus are equal)
Therefore, Triangle AOD is congruent to Triangle COD  (SSS congruence rule)
Step 3: This gives, angle AOD = angle COD  (CPCT)
But, angle AOD + angle COD = 180 degrees  (Linear pair)
So, 2 x angle AOD = 180 degrees
Or, angle AOD = 90 degrees.
ANSWER: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other.
EXAMPLE 8.1.3: Isosceles triangle and parallelogram
PROBLEM: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC. AD bisects exterior angle PAC and CD || AB. Show that (i) angle DAC = angle BCA and (ii) ABCD is a parallelogram.
SOLUTION:
(i) Proving angle DAC = angle BCA:
Step 1: Triangle ABC is isosceles in which AB = AC  (Given)
So, angle ABC = angle ACB  (Angles opposite to equal sides)
Step 2: angle PAC = angle ABC + angle ACB  (Exterior angle of a triangle)
Or, angle PAC = 2 x angle ACB  ... (1)
Step 3: AD bisects angle PAC.
So, angle PAC = 2 x angle DAC  ... (2)
Step 4: From (1) and (2): 2 x angle DAC = 2 x angle ACB
Therefore, angle DAC = angle ACB
(ii) Proving ABCD is a parallelogram:
Step 5: angle DAC = angle BCA are alternate angles when BC and AD are intersected by transversal AC.
So, BC || AD.
Step 6: Also, BA || CD  (Given)
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
ANSWER: (i) angle DAC = angle BCA  (ii) ABCD is a parallelogram.
EXAMPLE 8.1.4: Bisectors of interior angles form a rectangle
PROBLEM: Two parallel lines l and m are intersected by a transversal p. Show that the quadrilateral formed by the bisectors of interior angles is a rectangle.
SOLUTION:
Step 1: Given l || m and transversal p intersects l at A and m at C.
(PS is on line l passing through A; QR is on line m passing through C.)
The bisectors of angle PAC and angle ACQ meet at B.
The bisectors of angle ACR and angle SAC meet at D.
Step 2: Since l || m and p is a transversal:
angle PAC = angle ACR  (Alternate angles)
So, (1/2) angle PAC = (1/2) angle ACR
i.e., angle BAC = angle ACD
These are alternate angles for lines AB and DC with AC as transversal.
So, AB || DC.
Similarly, BC || AD  (Considering angles ACB and CAD)
Therefore, ABCD is a parallelogram.
Step 3: Also, angle PAC + angle CAS = 180 degrees  (Linear pair, PS is a straight line)
So, (1/2) angle PAC + (1/2) angle CAS = 90 degrees
angle BAC + angle CAD = 90 degrees
angle BAD = 90 degrees.
Step 4: ABCD is a parallelogram in which one angle is 90 degrees.
ANSWER: The quadrilateral ABCD formed by the angle bisectors is a rectangle.
EXAMPLE 8.1.5: Bisectors of angles of parallelogram form a rectangle
PROBLEM: Show that the bisectors of angles of a parallelogram form a rectangle.
SOLUTION:
Step 1: Let P, Q, R and S be the points of intersection of the bisectors of:
- angle A and angle B  (meet at P)
- angle B and angle C  (meet at Q)
- angle C and angle D  (meet at R)
- angle D and angle A  (meet at S)
of parallelogram ABCD.
Step 2: In Triangle ASD:
DS bisects angle D and AS bisects angle A.
angle DAS + angle ADS = (1/2) angle A + (1/2) angle D
= (1/2)(angle A + angle D)
= (1/2) x 180 degrees  (Co-interior angles, AD || BC)
= 90 degrees
Step 3: angle DAS + angle ADS + angle DSA = 180 degrees  (Angle sum of triangle)
So, 90 degrees + angle DSA = 180 degrees
angle DSA = 90 degrees
angle PSR = 90 degrees  (Vertically opposite to angle DSA)
Step 4: Similarly, angle SPQ = 90 degrees, angle PQR = 90 degrees, angle SRQ = 90 degrees.
Step 5: PQRS has all four angles equal to 90 degrees and opposite angles equal, so it is a parallelogram with one angle 90 degrees.
ANSWER: PQRS is a rectangle.
EXERCISES: (Exercise 8.1)
EXERCISE 8.1.1: If the diagonals of a parallelogram are equal, then show that it is a rectangle.
EXERCISE 8.1.2: Show that the diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

items.question: What is a parallelogram? State any two of its properties.
items.answer:
A PARALLELOGRAM is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
Properties:
(i)  Opposite sides are equal: AB = DC and AD = BC.  (Theorem 8.2)
(ii) Opposite angles are equal: angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.  (Theorem 8.4)

items.question: State Theorem 8.1. What congruence rule is used in its proof?
items.answer:
Theorem 8.1: A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles.
In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC gives:
Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
Congruence rule used: ASA (Angle-Side-Angle).
Reason: angle BCA = angle DAC (alternate angles, BC || AD),
AC = CA (common), angle BAC = angle DCA (alternate angles, AB || DC).

items.question: In rhombus ABCD, diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. What is angle AOB? Give reason.
items.answer:
In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at right angles.
Therefore, angle AOB = 90 degrees.
Reason: Proved using SSS congruence — In Triangle AOD and Triangle COD:
OA = OC (diagonals bisect), OD = OD (common), AD = CD (all sides of rhombus equal).
So Triangle AOD is congruent to Triangle COD, giving angle AOD = angle COD.
Since they form a linear pair: 2 x angle AOD = 180, so angle AOD = 90 degrees.

items.question: In parallelogram ABCD, if angle A = 70 degrees, find all four angles.
items.answer:
angle C = angle A = 70 degrees.  (Opposite angles are equal — Theorem 8.4)
angle A + angle B = 180 degrees.  (Co-interior angles, AD || BC)
angle B = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.
angle D = angle B = 110 degrees.  (Opposite angles are equal)
Answer: angle A = 70 degrees, angle B = 110 degrees, angle C = 70 degrees, angle D = 110 degrees.

---

items.question: Prove that in a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal. (Theorem 8.2)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a parallelogram.
TO PROVE: AB = DC and AD = BC.
PROOF:
Step 1: Draw diagonal AC.
Step 2: In Triangle ABC and Triangle CDA:
angle BCA = angle DAC  (Alternate angles, BC || AD, AC is transversal)
angle BAC = angle DCA  (Alternate angles, AB || DC, AC is transversal)
AC = CA  (Common side)
Step 3: By ASA rule: Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
Step 4: Therefore AB = DC and AD = BC.  (CPCT)
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: Prove that if the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then it is a parallelogram. (Theorem 8.7)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    In quadrilateral ABCD, diagonals AC and BD bisect each other at O.
So, OA = OC and OB = OD.
TO PROVE: ABCD is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AOB and Triangle COD:
OA = OC  (Given)
OB = OD  (Given)
angle AOB = angle COD  (Vertically opposite angles)
Step 2: By SAS rule: Triangle AOB is congruent to Triangle COD.
Step 3: Therefore angle OAB = angle OCD.  (CPCT)
These are alternate interior angles for lines AB and CD cut by transversal AC.
So, AB || CD.
Step 4: Similarly (using Triangles AOD and COB): BC || AD.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so ABCD is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.

---

items.question: Prove that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. (Theorem 8.6)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a parallelogram. Diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.
TO PROVE: OA = OC and OB = OD.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AOB and Triangle COD:
angle OAB = angle OCD  (Alternate angles, AB || DC and AC is transversal)
Step 2: angle OBA = angle ODC  (Alternate angles, AB || DC and BD is transversal)
Step 3: AB = CD  (Opposite sides of parallelogram are equal — Theorem 8.2)
Step 4: By ASA rule: Triangle AOB is congruent to Triangle COD.
Therefore OA = OC and OB = OD.  (CPCT)
Hence O is the mid-point of both diagonals; the diagonals bisect each other.
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: Show that the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.
items.answer:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a rhombus. Diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.
TO PROVE: OA = OC, OB = OD, and AC is perpendicular to BD.
PROOF:
Step 1: Since a rhombus is a parallelogram, its diagonals bisect each other.
Therefore, OA = OC and OB = OD.  (Theorem 8.6)
Step 2: In Triangle AOD and Triangle COD:
OA = OC  (Proved above)
OD = OD  (Common)
AD = CD  (All sides of a rhombus are equal)
Step 3: By SSS rule: Triangle AOD is congruent to Triangle COD.
Therefore, angle AOD = angle COD.  (CPCT)
Step 4: Since angle AOD and angle COD form a linear pair:
angle AOD + angle COD = 180 degrees.
2 x angle AOD = 180 degrees.
angle AOD = 90 degrees.
Therefore, AC is perpendicular to BD.
HENCE PROVED. Diagonals bisect each other at right angles.

items.question: Two parallel lines l and m are intersected by a transversal p. Show that the quadrilateral formed by the bisectors of the interior angles is a rectangle.
items.answer:
GIVEN:    l || m, transversal p meets l at A and m at C.
Bisectors of angle PAC and angle ACQ meet at B.
Bisectors of angle ACR and angle SAC meet at D.
TO PROVE: Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle.
PROOF:
Step 1: Since l || m and p is a transversal:
angle PAC = angle ACR  (Alternate interior angles)
(1/2) angle PAC = (1/2) angle ACR,  i.e., angle BAC = angle ACD.
These are alternate angles for AB and DC cut by AC.  So AB || DC.
Step 2: Similarly, considering angle ACB and angle CAD:  BC || AD.
Therefore ABCD is a parallelogram.
Step 3: angle PAC + angle CAS = 180 degrees.  (PS is a straight line — linear pair)
(1/2) angle PAC + (1/2) angle CAS = 90 degrees.
angle BAC + angle CAD = 90 degrees.
angle BAD = 90 degrees.
Step 4: ABCD is a parallelogram with one angle = 90 degrees.
Therefore ABCD is a rectangle.
HENCE PROVED.

---

items.question: (a) Prove that if each pair of opposite sides of a quadrilateral is equal, then it is a parallelogram. (Theorem 8.3)
items.answer:
PART A — Proof of Theorem 8.3:
GIVEN:    In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = CD and AD = BC.
TO PROVE: ABCD is a parallelogram.
CONSTRUCTION: Draw diagonal AC.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle ABC and Triangle CDA:
AB = CD  (Given)
AD = CB  (Given, AD = BC)
AC = CA  (Common side)
Step 2: By SSS rule: Triangle ABC is congruent to Triangle CDA.
Step 3: From CPCT: angle BAC = angle DCA and angle BCA = angle DAC.
Step 4: angle BAC = angle DCA are alternate interior angles for lines AB and DC with transversal AC.
So, AB || DC.
Step 5: angle BCA = angle DAC are alternate interior angles for lines BC and AD with transversal AC.
So, BC || AD.
Step 6: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
Therefore ABCD is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.

PART B — Proving AP = CQ:
GIVEN:    Parallelogram ABCD. P and Q on diagonal BD with DP = BQ.
TO PROVE: AP = CQ.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle APD and Triangle CQB:
AD = CB  (Opposite sides of parallelogram are equal)
Step 2: angle ADP = angle CBQ.
(AD || BC and BD is transversal — alternate interior angles)
Step 3: DP = BQ.  (Given)
Step 4: By SAS rule: Triangle APD is congruent to Triangle CQB.
Step 5: Therefore AP = CQ.  (CPCT)
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into:

options.A: Two equal but not necessarily congruent triangles
options.C: Two similar but not congruent triangles

items.answer: B
items.explanation: Theorem 8.1 states that a diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles (proved by ASA rule).

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, if angle A = 80 degrees, then angle C equals:
items.answer: B
items.explanation: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. So angle C = angle A = 80 degrees.

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, if angle A = 110 degrees, then angle B equals:
items.answer: B
items.explanation: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary. angle B = 180 - 110 = 70 degrees.

items.question: The diagonals of a parallelogram:

options.D: Bisect each other at right angles

items.answer: C
items.explanation: Theorem 8.6: diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other (not necessarily equal or perpendicular).

items.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a rectangle?

options.D: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles

items.answer: D
items.explanation: Diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other and are equal, but they are NOT perpendicular unless it is a square.

items.question: In a rhombus, the diagonals:

options.B: Bisect each other at right angles

items.answer: B
items.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (proved using SSS congruence in Example 8.1.2).

items.question: If in a quadrilateral ABCD, AB = CD and BC = AD, then ABCD is a:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: Theorem 8.3: if each pair of opposite sides is equal, then the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

items.question: In parallelogram ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. If OA = 5 cm, then OC equals:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. So OC = OA = 5 cm.

items.question: A parallelogram in which all four sides are equal is called a:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: A RHOMBUS is a parallelogram with all four sides equal. A square also has equal sides but additionally has all angles equal to 90 degrees.

items.question: In a square ABCD, the diagonals bisect each other at:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: Diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles (90 degrees) and are also equal in length.

items.question: Theorem 8.7 states that if the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then it is a parallelogram. This theorem is the:

options.A: Direct form of a new theorem

items.answer: B
items.explanation: Theorem 8.6 says "diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other." Theorem 8.7 reverses this condition — it is the converse of Theorem 8.6.

items.question: In rectangle ABCD, if angle A = 90 degrees, which reasoning correctly proves angle B = 90 degrees?

options.A: AD || BC with AB as transversal; co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees, so angle B = 90 degrees
options.B: Opposite angles of a rectangle are equal, so angle B = angle D = 90 degrees
options.C: All sides of a rectangle are equal
options.D: Diagonals of a rectangle are perpendicular

items.answer: A
items.explanation: Since AD || BC and AB is a transversal, angle A + angle B = 180 degrees (co-interior angles). Since angle A = 90 degrees, angle B = 90 degrees.

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
MID-POINT THEOREM: The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
MID-POINT: The point that divides a line segment into two equal halves.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Theorem 8.8: The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equals half of it.
Theorem 8.9: The line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side bisects the third side. (Converse of Theorem 8.8)
If E and F are mid-points of AB and AC in Triangle ABC, then EF || BC and EF = (1/2) BC.
Joining mid-points of all three sides of a triangle divides it into four congruent triangles.
The mid-point theorem is used to prove properties of quadrilaterals formed by joining mid-points of sides.

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - No sub-topics. (Book has only Topic 8.2 with no further sub-divisions.)
THEOREM: 8.8  (Mid-point Theorem)
STATEMENT: The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side.
GIVEN: In Triangle ABC, E and F are mid-points of AB and AC respectively.
TO PROVE: EF || BC and EF = (1/2) BC.
CONSTRUCTION: Through C, draw CD || BA. Extend EF to meet CD at D.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AEF and Triangle CDF:
angle AEF = angle CDF  (Alternate angles, BA || CD and EFD is a transversal)
angle AFE = angle CFD  (Vertically opposite angles)
AF = CF  (F is mid-point of AC, so AF = FC)
Step 2: Therefore, Triangle AEF is congruent to Triangle CDF  (ASA Rule)
Step 3: So, EF = DF  (CPCT) and AE = DC  (CPCT, since AE = EB)
Step 4: In quadrilateral BCDE:
BE || CD  (since BA || CD, and BE is part of BA)
BE = AE = DC  (proved above, since AE = EB and AE = DC)
Since one pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel, BCDE is a parallelogram.
Step 5: Therefore, EF || BC  (since ED || BC and F lies on ED).
Also, EF = (1/2) ED = (1/2) BC.
HENCE PROVED.
THEOREM: 8.9  (Converse of Mid-point Theorem)
STATEMENT: The line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side bisects the third side.
GIVEN: In Triangle ABC, E is the mid-point of AB. A line l through E is parallel to BC and meets AC at F.
TO PROVE: F is the mid-point of AC, i.e., AF = CF.
PROOF:
Step 1: Suppose F is NOT the mid-point of AC. Let F' be the actual mid-point.
By Theorem 8.8, EF' || BC.
Step 2: But we are given that EF || BC (line through E parallel to BC).
Step 3: Two lines EF and EF' both pass through E and are both parallel to BC.
This is possible only if F and F' are the same point.
Therefore, F is the mid-point of AC, i.e., AF = CF.
HENCE PROVED.
EXAMPLES: (Textbook Examples — Topic 8.2)
EXAMPLE 8.2.1: Triangle divided into four congruent triangles
PROBLEM: In Triangle ABC, D, E and F are respectively the mid-points of sides AB, BC and CA. Show that Triangle ABC is divided into four congruent triangles by joining D, E and F.
SOLUTION:
Step 1: D and E are mid-points of AB and BC.
By Theorem 8.8, DE || AC and DE = (1/2) AC.
Similarly, DF || BC and DF = (1/2) BC.
And EF || AB and EF = (1/2) AB.
Step 2: Since DE || AC (i.e., DE || AF) and DF || AB (i.e., DF || AE):
ADEF is a parallelogram. So, Triangle DAF is congruent to Triangle FED.
Similarly, BDFE is a parallelogram. So, Triangle BDE is congruent to Triangle FED.
Similarly, DFCE is a parallelogram. So, Triangle EFC is congruent to Triangle FED.
Step 3: So, all four triangles — Triangle BDE, Triangle DAF, Triangle EFC and Triangle DEF — are congruent to each other.
ANSWER: Triangle ABC is divided into four congruent triangles by joining D, E and F.
EXAMPLE 8.2.2: Equal intercepts on parallel transversals

PROBLEM: l, m and n are three parallel lines intersected by transversals p and q such that l, m and n cut off equal intercepts AB and BC on p. Show that l, m and n cut off equal intercepts DE and EF on q also.
SOLUTION:
Given: AB = BC on transversal p. Prove: DE = EF on transversal q.
Step 1: Join A to F. Let AF intersect line m at G.
Trapezium ACFD is divided into triangles ACF and AFD.
Step 2: In Triangle ACF:
B is the mid-point of AC  (AB = BC, given)
BG || CF  (since m || n, both BG and CF are segments of lines m and n)
By Theorem 8.9, G is the mid-point of AF.
Step 3: In Triangle AFD:
G is the mid-point of AF  (proved in Step 2)
GE || AD  (since l || m, both GE and AD are segments of lines m and l)
By Theorem 8.9, E is the mid-point of DF.
Therefore, DE = EF.
ANSWER: l, m and n cut off equal intercepts on transversal q also.
EXERCISES: (Exercise 8.2)

sections.label: EXERCISE 8.2.1: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which P, Q, R and S are mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA. AC is a diagonal. Show that:
sections.raw:
(i)   SR || AC and SR = (1/2) AC,
(ii)  PQ = SR,
(iii) PQRS is a parallelogram.

EXERCISE 8.2.2: ABCD is a rhombus and P, Q, R and S are the mid-points of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. Show that the quadrilateral PQRS is a rectangle.

EXERCISE 8.2.3: ABCD is a rectangle and P, Q, R and S are mid-points of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. Show that the quadrilateral PQRS is a rhombus.

EXERCISE 8.2.4: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB || DC, BD is a diagonal and E is the mid-point of AD. A line is drawn through E parallel to AB intersecting BC at F. Show that F is the mid-point of BC.

EXERCISE 8.2.5: In a parallelogram ABCD, E and F are the mid-points of sides AB and CD respectively. Show that the line segments AF and EC trisect the diagonal BD.

sections.label: EXERCISE 8.2.6: ABC is a triangle right angled at C. A line through the mid-point M of hypotenuse AB and parallel to BC intersects AC at D. Show that:
sections.raw:
(i)   D is the mid-point of AC,
(ii)  MD is perpendicular to AC,
(iii) CM = MA = (1/2) AB.

items.question: State the Mid-point Theorem. (Theorem 8.8)
items.answer:
Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.8):
The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
In Triangle ABC, if E and F are mid-points of AB and AC respectively, then:
EF || BC  and  EF = (1/2) BC.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, E and F are mid-points of AB and AC. If BC = 14 cm, find EF.
items.answer:
Given: E and F are mid-points of AB and AC. BC = 14 cm.
By the Mid-point Theorem:
EF = (1/2) x BC = (1/2) x 14 = 7 cm.
Answer: EF = 7 cm.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D and E are mid-points of AB and AC. If DE = 5.5 cm, find BC.
items.answer:
Given: D and E are mid-points of AB and AC. DE = 5.5 cm.
By the Mid-point Theorem: DE = (1/2) BC.
So, BC = 2 x DE = 2 x 5.5 = 11 cm.
Answer: BC = 11 cm.

items.question: State Theorem 8.9. How is it related to Theorem 8.8?
items.answer:
Theorem 8.9 (Converse of Mid-point Theorem):
The line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.
Relation: Theorem 8.9 is the converse of Theorem 8.8.
Theorem 8.8 says: mid-points joined → line is parallel and half.
Theorem 8.9 says: line through mid-point, parallel to a side → bisects the third side.

---

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D, E, F are mid-points of AB, BC and CA respectively. If the perimeter of Triangle ABC is 24 cm, find the perimeter of Triangle DEF. Also name all the parallelograms formed.
items.answer:
Step 1: Given: perimeter of Triangle ABC = AB + BC + CA = 24 cm.
Step 2: By Mid-point Theorem in Triangle ABC:
DE || CA  and  DE = (1/2) CA.
EF || AB  and  EF = (1/2) AB.
DF || BC  and  DF = (1/2) BC.
Step 3: Perimeter of Triangle DEF = DE + EF + DF
= (1/2)CA + (1/2)AB + (1/2)BC
= (1/2)(AB + BC + CA)
= (1/2) x 24 = 12 cm.
Step 4: Parallelograms formed: ADEF, BDFE, DFCE.
Answer: Perimeter of Triangle DEF = 12 cm.

items.question: Prove: The line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side bisects the third side. (Theorem 8.9)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    In Triangle ABC, E is the mid-point of AB.
Line l through E is parallel to BC and meets AC at F.
TO PROVE: F is the mid-point of AC, i.e., AF = CF.
PROOF:
Step 1: Suppose F is NOT the mid-point of AC.
Let F' be the true mid-point of AC.
Step 2: By Theorem 8.8 (Mid-point Theorem):
E and F' are mid-points of AB and AC respectively.
So, EF' || BC.
Step 3: But we are given that EF || BC.
Both lines EF and EF' pass through E and are parallel to BC.
Step 4: Through a point, only one line can be drawn parallel to a given line.
Therefore F and F' must coincide, i.e., F = F'.
Hence, F is the mid-point of AC.
HENCE PROVED.

---

items.question: Prove the Mid-point Theorem: The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it. (Theorem 8.8)
items.answer:
GIVEN:    In Triangle ABC, E and F are mid-points of AB and AC respectively.
TO PROVE: EF || BC  and  EF = (1/2) BC.
CONSTRUCTION: Through C, draw CD || BA. Extend EF to meet CD at D.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle AEF and Triangle CDF:
angle AEF = angle CDF  (Alternate interior angles, BA || CD, EFD is transversal)
AF = CF  (F is mid-point of AC)
angle AFE = angle CFD  (Vertically opposite angles)
Step 2: By ASA rule: Triangle AEF is congruent to Triangle CDF.
Step 3: Therefore EF = DF  (CPCT)  and  AE = DC.  (CPCT)
Since AE = EB (E is mid-point): DC = BE.
Step 4: In quadrilateral BCDE: BE || CD (part of BA || CD) and BE = DC.
One pair of opposite sides equal and parallel → BCDE is a parallelogram.
Step 5: Therefore EF || BC  (since ED || BC and F lies on ED).
Also, EF = (1/2) ED = (1/2) BC.
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D, E and F are mid-points of sides AB, BC and CA respectively. Show that Triangle ABC is divided into four congruent triangles by joining D, E and F.
items.answer:
GIVEN:    In Triangle ABC, D, E and F are mid-points of AB, BC and CA respectively.
TO PROVE: The four triangles — Triangle BDE, Triangle ADF, Triangle EFC and Triangle DEF — are all congruent.
PROOF:
Step 1: By Mid-point Theorem (Theorem 8.8):
DE || AC  and  DE = (1/2) AC.   (D, E mid-points of AB, BC)
DF || BC  and  DF = (1/2) BC.   (D, F mid-points of AB, CA)
EF || AB  and  EF = (1/2) AB.   (E, F mid-points of BC, CA)
Step 2: Since DE || AC (i.e., DE || AF) and DF || AB (i.e., DF || AE):
ADEF is a parallelogram.
Since BDFE is a parallelogram: diagonal DE divides it → Triangle BDE is congruent to Triangle FED.
Step 3: Since ADEF is a parallelogram: Triangle ADF is congruent to Triangle FED.
Since DFCE is a parallelogram: Triangle EFC is congruent to Triangle FED.
Step 4: All four triangles — Triangle BDE, Triangle ADF, Triangle EFC, Triangle DEF — are congruent to each other.
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB || DC. BD is a diagonal and E is the mid-point of AD. A line through E, parallel to AB, intersects BC at F. Show that F is the mid-point of BC.
items.answer:
GIVEN:    Trapezium ABCD with AB || DC. E is mid-point of AD.
Line through E parallel to AB meets BC at F.
TO PROVE: F is the mid-point of BC.
PROOF:
Step 1: Let the line through E (parallel to AB) intersect BD at G.
Step 2: In Triangle ABD:
E is the mid-point of AD and EG || AB  (since the line is parallel to AB).
By Theorem 8.9 (Converse of Mid-point Theorem):
G is the mid-point of BD.
Step 3: In Triangle BDC:
G is the mid-point of BD  (proved above)
GF || DC  (since EF || AB || DC — all three are parallel)
By Theorem 8.9:
F is the mid-point of BC.
HENCE PROVED.

---

items.question: (a) ABCD is a quadrilateral in which P, Q, R and S are mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. AC is a diagonal. Prove that PQRS is a parallelogram.
items.answer:
PART A — Proving PQRS is a parallelogram:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a quadrilateral. P, Q, R, S are mid-points of AB, BC, CD, DA. AC is a diagonal.
TO PROVE: PQRS is a parallelogram.
PROOF:
Step 1: In Triangle ABC, P and Q are mid-points of AB and BC respectively.
By Theorem 8.8 (Mid-point Theorem):
PQ || AC  and  PQ = (1/2) AC.    ...(1)
Step 2: In Triangle ACD, S and R are mid-points of AD and CD respectively.
By Theorem 8.8 (Mid-point Theorem):
SR || AC  and  SR = (1/2) AC.    ...(2)
Step 3: From (1) and (2): PQ || SR  and  PQ = SR.
Step 4: In quadrilateral PQRS, one pair of opposite sides (PQ and SR) is both equal and parallel.
Therefore PQRS is a parallelogram.
HENCE PROVED.

PART B — Proving PQRS is a rectangle when ABCD is a rhombus:
GIVEN:    ABCD is a rhombus (so all sides are equal and diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular).
TO PROVE: PQRS is a rectangle.
PROOF:
Step 1: From Part A, PQRS is a parallelogram.
Step 2: In Triangle ABD, P and S are mid-points of AB and AD respectively.
By Theorem 8.8: PS || BD  and  PS = (1/2) BD.     ...(3)
Step 3: From (1): PQ || AC  and  from (3): PS || BD.
Since the diagonals AC and BD of a rhombus are perpendicular (angle between them = 90 degrees):
PQ is perpendicular to PS.
That is, angle QPS = 90 degrees.
Step 4: In parallelogram PQRS, one angle = 90 degrees.
Therefore PQRS is a rectangle.
HENCE PROVED.

items.question: The Mid-point Theorem states that the line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is:

options.A: Equal to the third side and perpendicular to it
options.B: Parallel to the third side and half of it
options.C: Parallel to the third side and equal to it
options.D: Half of the third side and perpendicular to it

items.answer: B
items.explanation: Theorem 8.8: The line joining mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is (1/2) of it.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, E and F are mid-points of AB and AC. If BC = 10 cm, then EF equals:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: By Mid-point Theorem, EF = (1/2) x BC = (1/2) x 10 = 5 cm.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, D, E, F are mid-points of AB, BC, CA respectively. How many congruent triangles are formed by joining D, E, F?
items.answer: C
items.explanation: Joining mid-points of all three sides divides Triangle ABC into four congruent triangles: Triangle BDE, Triangle DAF, Triangle EFC and Triangle DEF.

items.question: Theorem 8.9 is the converse of Theorem 8.8. It states that the line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side:

options.B: Is equal to the third side
options.C: Is perpendicular to the third side

items.answer: A
items.explanation: Theorem 8.9: A line through the mid-point of one side, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, E is the mid-point of AB. A line through E parallel to BC meets AC at F. Then F is:
items.answer: B
items.explanation: By Theorem 8.9, a line through mid-point of one side parallel to another side bisects the third side. So F is the mid-point of AC.

items.question: ABCD is a quadrilateral. P, Q, R, S are mid-points of AB, BC, CD, DA. What is the figure PQRS?
items.answer: C
items.explanation: PQ || AC and PQ = (1/2)AC (by Theorem 8.8 in Triangle ABC). SR || AC and SR = (1/2)AC (in Triangle ACD). So PQ || SR and PQ = SR. Hence PQRS is a parallelogram.

items.question: In Triangle ABC, if EF joins mid-points of AB and AC, and EF = 5 cm, then BC equals:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: By Mid-point Theorem, EF = (1/2) BC. So BC = 2 x EF = 2 x 5 = 10 cm.

items.question: ABCD is a rhombus and P, Q, R, S are mid-points of AB, BC, CD, DA. The figure PQRS is:
items.answer: B
items.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. The sides of PQRS are parallel to the diagonals, so all angles of PQRS are 90 degrees. Hence PQRS is a rectangle.

items.question: ABCD is a rectangle and P, Q, R, S are mid-points of AB, BC, CD, DA respectively. The figure PQRS is:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal. The sides of PQRS are parallel to and equal to half of the diagonals, so all four sides of PQRS are equal. Hence PQRS is a rhombus.

items.question: Three parallel lines l, m, n cut a transversal p at A, B, C such that AB = BC. Another transversal q is cut at D, E, F. Then:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: By Example 8.2.2 (using Theorem 8.9), equal intercepts on one transversal imply equal intercepts on any other transversal. So DE = EF.

items.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, E and F are mid-points of AB and CD respectively. The line segments AF and EC trisect the diagonal:
items.answer: B
items.explanation: As proved in Exercise 8.2.5, AF and EC trisect diagonal BD. The three equal parts are BP = PQ = QD where P and Q are the intersection points.

items.question: The congruence rule used to prove Theorem 8.8 (Mid-point Theorem) is:
items.answer: C
items.explanation: In the proof of Theorem 8.8, Triangle AEF is congruent to Triangle CDF using ASA rule — angle AEF = angle CDF (alternate angles), AF = FC (F is mid-point of AC), angle AFE = angle CFD (vertically opposite angles).

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text: This topic summarises all key results proved in Chapter 8 on Quadrilaterals.

sections.label: Key Points (Summary):
points: 1. A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles.
2. In a parallelogram:
(i)  opposite sides are equal
(ii) opposite angles are equal
(iii) diagonals bisect each other
3. Diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other and are equal — and vice-versa.
4. Diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles — and vice-versa.
5. Diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles and are equal — and vice-versa.
6. The line-segment joining the mid-points of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
7. A line through the mid-point of a side of a triangle parallel to another side bisects the third side.

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - No sub-topics. (8.3 is a summary section only.)
